competition: Kyrgyzstan Republican Mathematical Olympiad — Final (Stage IV)

problems.problem: Wrestlers from the villages of Orto-Suu and Kyzyl-Dyikan took part in an alysh tournament. There were $9$ more wrestlers from Orto-Suu than from Kyzyl-Dyikan. Every wrestler competed against every other wrestler; a win earned $1$ point and a loss $0$ points. The wrestlers from Orto-Suu scored in total $9$ times as many points as those from Kyzyl-Dyikan. What is the greatest possible total number of points scored by the wrestlers from Kyzyl-Dyikan?
The medians drawn from vertices $A$ and $B$ of triangle $ABC$ are perpendicular. Prove that $AB$ is the shortest side of triangle $ABC$.
Find all triples of natural numbers $(x,y,z)$ satisfying $$1+4^x+4^y=z^2.$$
Prove that for positive numbers $a,b,c$, $$\frac{a^2}{b}+\frac{b^3}{c^2}+\frac{c^4}{a^3}\ge -a+2b+2c.$$
Let $x,y,z$ be positive numbers such that $x^n,y^n,z^n$ are the side lengths of a triangle for every natural number $n$. Determine all such triangles.
Find the integer part of $$\frac{2^1}{1!}+\frac{2^2}{2!}+\cdots+\frac{2^{2018}}{2018!},$$ where the integer part of a number $\alpha$ is the greatest integer not exceeding $\alpha$.

In the multiplication С × НОВЫМ = ГОДОМ, equal digits have been replaced by equal letters and different digits by different letters. The original Cyrillic letters are retained. (a) Find the digit represented by Н. (b) Find the digit represented by every letter.
Find one or two different formulas for a function $f$ with the values $f(-1)=1$, $f(0)=3$, $f(1)=1$, $f(2)=3$.

(a) Find all noncongruent tetrahedra whose five edges have lengths $19,19,10,10,10$, and whose sixth edge has length $19$ or $10$. (b) Find the volume of one of the resulting tetrahedra and round it up to an integer.
Find all solutions in natural numbers of $$x^2+1^0+y^1+z^9=2019.$$

Square $ABCD$ has side length $18$. Points $K$ on $AB$ and $L$ on $AD$ are chosen so that triangle $AKL$ has perimeter $18$. Point $M$ on $BC$ is chosen so that $LM$ is parallel to $AB$. Point $N$ on $DC$ is chosen so that $KN$ is parallel to $AD$. Find the area of triangle $CNM$.

A “word” must contain each of the Cyrillic letters Ч, Ы, Н, Б, О, Ж, Т exactly once. Only the following pairs of adjacent letters are allowed: БО, ОБ, ОЖ, ЖО, ОН, НО, ЖТ, ТЖ, ЖЧ, ЧЖ, ЖН, НЖ, ЧТ, ТЧ, ЧН, НЧ, ЧЫ, ЫЧ, НЫ, ЫН. An example is ЫЧТЖНОБ. (a) What could these letters and “words” represent? (b) How many different such “words” are there?
Prove that among the natural numbers whose decimal representations contain only the digit $1$, there is a multiple of $991$.
A function $g$ is defined for all real $x\ne1$ and satisfies $$2g\left(\frac{x}{x-1}\right)+\frac{x+1}{x-1}=3g(x).$$ (a) Find $g(3)$ and $g(\frac32)$. (b) Find all functions satisfying the condition.

In an acute triangle $ABC$, $AC=1$ and $\angle BAC=\alpha$. Three disks of radius $1$ are centred at the vertices $A,B,C$. Prove that if $AB\le\cos\alpha+\sqrt3\sin\alpha$, then these disks cover the whole triangle.

There are $c$ blue points and $k$ red points placed in an arbitrary order on a circle. Between two neighbouring blue points write $2$, between two neighbouring red points write $\frac12$, and between two neighbouring points of different colours write $1$. What is the product of all the numbers written?

The first term of a sequence $(x_k)$ is $0$, and for every $k\ge2$ it satisfies $$|x_k|=|x_{k-1}+2|.$$ (a) Prove that if $A_n$ is the arithmetic mean of the first $n$ terms, then $A_n\ge-1$ for every positive integer $n$. (b) Give an example of such a sequence for which $A_p=-1$ for some $p$.

Three vertices of a rhombus lie respectively on sides $AB,BC,AD$ of a square $ABCD$. What figure is formed by the set of all possible fourth vertices of these rhombi? Find its area when the square has side length $2$.
Let $f_0(x)=\cos(\pi x)$ and $f_n(x)=f_0(f_{n-1}(x))$. (a) Solve $f_2(x)=1$. (b) How many distinct real solutions does $f_{2023}(x)=x$ have?
A convex cyclic quadrilateral $ABCD$ satisfies $AB+CD=AD$. A circle $w$ is tangent to its three sides $AB,BC,CD$. Prove that the centre of $w$ lies on side $AD$.
Prove that $$\{\sqrt1\}+\{\sqrt2\}+\{\sqrt3\}+\cdots+\{\sqrt{2023^2}\}\le\frac{2023^2-1}{2},$$ where $\{x\}$ denotes the fractional part of $x$.

Consider the equation $$y(y(r)+y(z))=k\,y(r)+g\,y(z),$$ where $k,g$ are constants. (a) Find $y(2023)$ if $y(0)=0$ and $y(1)=1$. (b) Find all functions $y:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$ satisfying the equation for which distinct arguments have distinct function values.

In an acute triangle $ABC$ with $AB=BC$, the circumcentre $O$ and incentre $V$ lie inside the triangle. Point $X$ on side $BC$ is chosen so that $VX$ is parallel to $AB$. Prove that $OX$ and $CV$ are perpendicular.
Ten football players are standing in a row. In how many ways can they be rearranged so that the player to the left of each player is different from the player who was previously to their left?
Express $2024$ as a sum of consecutive natural numbers. Find all such representations.
How many real roots does the equation $$x-100\sin x-10=0$$ have? Justify your answer.

A circle passing through vertices $A,B$ and the midpoint $D$ of side $AC$ of a triangle $ABC$ meets side $BC$ at $E$. A second circle passes through $E$ and is tangent to line $AB$ at $B$. Line $DE$ meets the second circle again at $F$ and meets line $AB$ at $G$. Prove that lines $BF,AE,CG$ are concurrent.

Find all solutions of the system $$\begin{cases}ax+by+ct=0,\\dx+ey+ft=0,\\kx+my+pt=0,\end{cases}$$ where the sum of the coefficients in each equation is positive, $a,e,p$ are positive, and all the other coefficients are negative.
Two planes divide a cube into four parts of equal volume. Prove that these planes also divide the surface of the cube into four parts of equal area.

A classroom has three rows of desks, with four desks in each row. Two pupils must sit at each occupied desk for pair work. In how many ways can a teacher seat nine girls and nine boys if each boy must share a desk with a girl, Meerim must sit at a front desk, and Ruslan must sit in the left-hand row?

Initially all cells of a magical $5000\times70$ grid are grey. A painter stands on some cell and paints it red. Each second the painter takes two steps, one cell to the left and one cell down, and paints red the cell reached after both steps. A leftward step from the leftmost column takes the painter to the rightmost cell of the same row; a downward step from the bottom row takes the painter to the topmost cell of the same column. After some moves the painter returns to the starting cell. How many cells are red at that moment?
If $x^2+bx+c=0$ has two distinct real roots, how many distinct real roots does $$x^4-bx^3+(c-2)x^2+bx+1=0$$ have? Justify your answer.

Sides $AB,BC,AC$ of a triangle $ABC$ touch its incircle at $C_1,A_1,B_1$, respectively. The bisector of $\angle B_1A_1C_1$ meets line $m$, which contains the midsegment of triangle $A_1B_1C_1$ parallel to $B_1C_1$, at $K$. Prove that the circumcircle of triangle $BCK$ is tangent to $m$.

Ninety people sit around a large round table facing its centre: $40$ khans, $30$ beks and $20$ manaps. At a signal, all those whose left and right neighbours have the same title must stand up simultaneously. For example, a bek stands if both neighbours have the same title, which need not be bek. What is the largest possible number of people who can stand up? Justify your answer.
Consider all trapezoids of area $1$ whose diagonals have lengths $d_1,d_2$ with $d_1\ge d_2$. What is the smallest possible value of $d_1$?

A class has $20$ pupils. Any two pupils are either friends or are not friends. Friends can copy homework from each other, and pupils who are not friends cannot. The teacher knows that if any single pupil does the homework, then by the next lesson everyone will have done it. Prove that six pupils can be selected so that every other pupil is either a friend of one of these six or a friend of a friend of one of them.
